daily.title: Trump signs 'tremendous' Greenland security deal
daily.summary: Donald Trump strikes a security deal with Greenland and Denmark on the sidelines of the UN General Assembly. The deal comes after Trump repeatedly said the US should own the Danish territory.

daily.title: EU drops sanctions for Russian oligarchs Usmanov and Fridman
daily.summary: France and Luxembourg were behind the sanctions exemptions for Alisher Usmanov and Mikhail Fridman, a move that Kyiv labeled "shameful and unjustifiable."

daily.title: Amateur archeologist unearths Germany's largest trove of Roman coins
daily.summary: What began as a routine search in a field near Wesseling led to the discovery of nearly 1,000 Roman silver coins, one of the most significant archaeological finds in Germany in recent years.

daily.title: Military aircraft crashes near US air base in Spangdahlem, Germany
daily.summary: The F-16 pilot was able to safely eject from the plane and was taken to receive medical care. The incident occurred near Spangdahlem Air Base in the German state of Rhineland-Palatinate.

daily.title: US-China AI race: Does Trump want to regulate AI by forming a new task force and a special envoy for artificial intelligence in the US?
daily.summary: Do Trump's task force and a special envoy for artificial intelligence in the US indicate a move toward regulating this disputed technology, particularly vis-a-vis China?

daily.title: Young Berliners vote overwhelmingly for socialist Left  Party
daily.summary: Berlin's young voters overwhelmingly supported the victorious socialist Left Party. Are the young more radical? Or are the election results just a reflection of current German politics?

daily.title: Living in the shadow of LA's hidden oil wells
daily.summary: Many lifelong residents of Los Angeles have health impacts from growing up close to oil extraction. Now, the city is trying to close down the worst offenders, but it's an enormous task.

daily.title: After floods, Nepal minister demands 'climate justice'
daily.summary: With Nepal still reeling from the devastating floods in August, Kathmandu is calling for climate justice and seeking compensation from the UN-backed Loss and Damage Fund, Environment Minister Geeta Chaudhary told DW.

daily.title: Could we see MMA at the Olympics?
daily.summary: Mixed martial arts has made its debut at the Asian Games this week. It takes the sport closer to the Olympics but there are doubts about the next step, and the influence of the popular and lucrative UFC.

daily.title: Iran war spreads through region as Trump seeks way out
daily.summary: Washington, Tehran and the Gulf states continue to pursue different objectives while searching for a way to end the Iran war.

daily.title: Turkey: Several pupils injured in shooting outside school
daily.summary: The shooter, a pupil, allegedly took a rifle and shot indiscriminately at his schoolmates in front of their high school. Turkey was shocked by two back-to-back school shootings earlier this year.

daily.title: Russia, Ukraine trade deadly strikes as Zelenskyy attends UNGA
daily.summary: The Russian army targeted economic infrastructure in Ukraine, while Ukraine struck an oil refinery. This comes ahead of the UN General Assembly, where President Volodymyr Zelenskyy is due to meet Trump on the sidelines.

daily.title: Male infertility is 'grossly underreported'
daily.summary: It's not all on women anymore — doctors do test men for sperm count and motility. But still too few men get checked, possibly due to a misconception that a healthy sex life means healthy sperm. Spoiler: It doesn't.

daily.title: UN General Assembly opens with Macron, Trump, Erdogan, Lula, others in NYC
daily.summary: Donald Trump hailed his own record and hinted at a chance for peace in Iran and Ukraine. Turkey's president called for more pressure on Israel. UN leaders called for more global interdependence. DW has the latest.

daily.title: 'Swan Song': New book by Princess Diana's brother drops
daily.summary: A memoir penned by Charles Spencer on his older sister's life has been released, opening old royal wounds nearly three decades after Princess Diana's death.

daily.title: Will Germany have enough gas this winter amid energy supply crunch?
daily.summary: Germany's gas storage sites are far less full than in recent years. Officials say supplies are secure, but analysts warn that a cold winter or import disruptions could push prices higher. So how secure is the supply?

daily.title: Germany news: VW to step up cost-cutting program
daily.summary: Volkswagen's chief says the carmaker will accelerate its streamlining measures as workers protest. The Israeli ambassador says the Left Party win in Berlin polls poses a risk to the city's Jewish community. DW has more.

daily.title: How will Germany's Merz respond after crushing state election results and losses to the far right?
daily.summary: Germany's far-right AfD and the socialist Left Party gained ground in recent state elections, while the centrist parties lost support. The biggest loser is Chancellor Friedrich Merz.

daily.title: Princess Diana's brother makes explosive claims about royals in new memoir
daily.summary: Here are some of the key revelations from Charles Earl Spencer's highly anticipated memoir "Swan Song: Diana, My Sister." It has already provoked Buckingham Palace to react.

daily.title: India news: Police investigate alleged gang-rape in Delhi
daily.summary: While India is fuming over a viral video of two minors being harassed in Bihar, a case of an alleged gang-rape of a minor has emerged in a posh Delhi neighborhood. Meanwhile, India's foreign minister is at the UNGA.

weekly.title: Germany news: Trial starts of ex-Transport Minister Scheuer
weekly.summary: Former Transport Minister Andreas Scheuer is being tried for perjury related to a failed car toll scheme. And cherry farmers have brought in a bumper harvest.

weekly.title: Germany's car crisis: Can the 35-hour workweek survive?
weekly.summary: German carmakers want employees to work 40 hours instead of the current 35 without extra pay, arguing it would improve competitiveness. Unions strongly oppose the proposal and view it as an attack on workers' rights.

weekly.title: German state elections deal a blow to Chancellor Friedrich Merz
weekly.summary: Elections in Berlin and Mecklenburg-Western Pomerania have dealt the CDU a historic defeat while the AfD saw a massive gain. The pressure on Germany's unpopular chancellor is mounting.

weekly.title: AfD makes gains in state elections but has no government options
weekly.summary: Despite making significant gains in both Berlin and Mecklenburg-Western Pomerania, the far-right AfD remains without options to form a state government.

weekly.title: Germany faces energy tax losses as EV sales rise
weekly.summary: The rapid shift to electric vehicles in Germany is cutting fuel tax revenue for the government. As EV sales surge, policymakers face growing pressure to find new ways to fund roads and transportation infrastructure.

weekly.title: In cosmopolitan Berlin, elections still closed to foreigners
weekly.summary: A quarter of Berlin residents will have no say in the German capital's city-state election because they lack citizenship. That's the highest proportion of residents excluded from the election yet, and many are unhappy.

weekly.title: Germany news: Doctors offer Oktoberfest flu jabs
weekly.summary: Oktoberfest 2026 is underway but it's not just beer on offer in Munich this year; revelers can also get themselves a flu jab before heading to the tents. DW has more.

weekly.title: Germany: Is it possible to replace the chancellor?
weekly.summary: Chancellor Friedrich Merz's record-low approval ratings have emboldened his opponents. There are three ways to remove a chancellor from office in Germany.

weekly.title: Summer of 2026 broke records in Europe, and caused deaths
weekly.summary: The summer of 2026 was not only the hottest on record in Europe, it also saw a record number of people die. More than 16,000 are thought to have died because of the heat in Germany alone.

weekly.title: German-Russian relations at freezing point
weekly.summary: Russia's full-scale invasion of Ukraine destroyed the once-close relationship between Moscow and Berlin. Yet the far-right AfD is calling for a normalization of relations.

weekly.title: Ukraine steps up measures to protect railways
weekly.summary: As Russia increases its attacks on Ukraine's rail infrastructure, the Ukrainian government has called for help to replace destroyed locomotives and is making plans to keep passengers safe.

weekly.title: Mecklenburg-Western Pomerania: Will economy shape the vote?
weekly.summary: Voters in the eastern state of Mecklenburg-Western Pomerania head to the polls on Sunday, with the Social Democrats and far-right AfD neck and neck. Here's a look at key economic issues that could influence the election.

weekly.title: Oktoberfest 2026: Everything you need to know
weekly.summary: This year, AI will be used to manage overcrowded situations. Find all the numbers surrounding the fest — including the price of water!

weekly.title: Rebels, workers, radicals: The making of 'Red Berlin'
weekly.summary: Bloody May, student sit-ins and the squatter movement: Berlin has long been a hotbed for working-class organizing and radical left-wing politics.

weekly.title: Mecklenburg-Western Pomerania: SPD seeks to fend off AfD
weekly.summary: For nearly three decades, the Social Democrats have governed Germany's northeastern state. If they can fend off the AfD, the result may boost the fortunes of the German government's junior coalition partner.

weekly.title: Ever more Israelis moving to and investing in Cyprus
weekly.summary: Over the past three years, more and more Israelis have been purchasing property and investing in Cyprus, with many moving to the island permanently. How has this changed the Cypriot economy and how are locals responding?

weekly.title: Women's football in Germany booming, but still much to do
weekly.summary: Women's football is growing rapidly, particularly in Germany. Nevertheless, equal pay and investment remain major talking points.

weekly.title: Strait of Hormuz attacks spill oil into Persian Gulf
weekly.summary: As war disrupts one of the world's busiest shipping lanes, satellite images reveal that oil is spreading toward protected coral reefs and mangrove forests.

weekly.title: Airport malaria in Germany remains infrequent
weekly.summary: An outbreak of malaria at Frankfurt Airport this summer has raised alarm. Experts believe parasites probably arrived in a passenger's luggage. But with the onset of fall, the risks of contracting the disease are low.

weekly.title: Fact Check: False video alleges Berlin votes destroyed
weekly.summary: A video claiming to show AfD postal ballots being destroyed has gone viral ahead of Berlin's September 20 election. DW Fact Check examines the footage, the accounts sharing it and how widely it is really being viewed.

weekly.title: German police probe arson attack on Wuppertal synagogue
weekly.summary: The man detained shortly after allegedly trying to set fire to Wuppertal's synagogue made antisemitic comments to the arresting officers, prosecutors say. The 37-year-old Afghan citizen also had knives in his apartment.

weekly.title: Canada and EU: A look at the bloc's special relationships
weekly.summary: Though Canada may be some distance from Europe geographically, closer political ties are in the cards. With talk of an associate membership, DW takes a look at other arrangements the EU has with particular countries.

weekly.title: Dual citizenship means Germany now in competition for talent
weekly.summary: Coach Jürgen Klopp has named several players to his first Germany squad who are eligible to play for other countries. Some still aren't committed to playing for thje national team long-term.

weekly.title: Beethoven and Andy Warhol: Rebel icons on show in Bonn
weekly.summary: The new exhibition "Beethoven by Warhol" at the Beethoven House in Bonn presents the pop artist's late masterpiece: a picture of Ludwig van Beethoven. The exhibition shares the story of the work with the public.

weekly.title: 'No compromises': Far-right AfD has few potential partners
weekly.summary: Germany's far-right AfD party is riding high after its latest electoral triumph in Saxony-Anhalt. But one question remains: Does it actually want to govern?

weekly.title: VAR's mission creep a problem for football
weekly.summary: After a decade of use, questions around VAR in football are louder than ever. Has the technology strayed too far from its remit?

weekly.title: Organized crime and drug-related deaths rise Germany
weekly.summary: In the annual report on organized crime, German police say cocaine is a danger for the state and society and cases of money laundering have increased.

weekly.title: Russian birth tourism to Brazil increases
weekly.summary: Since Russia's full-scale invasion of Ukraine and stricter regulations in Argentina, more and more Russians are choosing to travel to Brazil to give birth to children, who will obtain Brazilian nationality.

weekly.title: A war-fatigued and anxious Russia picks a new parliament
weekly.summary: Fuel shortages, drone strikes and mobilization rumors are fueling anxiety and war fatigue in Russia. As support for peace talks grows among Russians, the Kremlin is watching closely ahead of parliamentary elections.

weekly.title: Alexander Ovechkin backs Putin party in campaign video
weekly.summary: Ice hockey legend Alexander Ovechkin has lent Vladimir Putin's party a helping hand in its parliamentary election campaign. That's in keeping with a pattern of support by an athlete who claims not to be political.

weekly.title: Judges: As AfD ascends, Germany must bolster justice system
weekly.summary: German judges and prosecutors warn that the coalition needs to reform the laws covering state prosecutors to prevent "extremists in government" from abusing the legal system.

weekly.title: As global crises grow, Germany cuts development aid
weekly.summary: The budget of Germany's Economic Cooperation and Development Ministry is set to shrink for the fifth consecutive year. Aid organizations warn that the cuts will have severe consequences for millions of people.

weekly.title: Klopp wants Germany's football team to 'reclaim the flag'
weekly.summary: Jürgen Klopp, Germany's new head coach, says he wants his team to reclaim pride in being German after recent political developments.

weekly.title: Serbian President Vucic criticizes Kosovo war crimes verdict
weekly.summary: The conviction of four former Kosovo Liberation Army leaders has drawn sharply different reactions across the Balkans. Serbia has accused the court of failing to fully address crimes against Serbs.

weekly.title: King Charles, Earl Spencer clash over Diana death once again
weekly.summary: Buckingham Palace has rejected criticism of King Charles III in a new book by the brother of his late wife, Princess Diana. Earl Charles Spencer has been a fierce critic of his former brother-in-law for decades.

weekly.title: Jews once lived lived here: When houses tell stories
weekly.summary: Time and again, residents tracing the history of their homes discover the lives of Jewish predecessors who fled or were deported amid stories of suffering and loss.

weekly.title: Jürgen Klopp's first Germany squad includes 44 players
weekly.summary: Germany's new head coach Jürgen Klopp has named a huge squad for his first four games, splitting them into two groups. A host of new faces is included.

weekly.title: Saint, sinner or feminist icon: How Mary Magdalene's image evolved through time
weekly.summary: From "Apostle of the Apostles" to prostitute, Mary Magdalene has been assigned a wide variety of roles, as a new exhibition shows.

weekly.title: How climate change worsened Nepal's deadly mountain collapse
weekly.summary: A glacier and rock collapse in Nepal killed nearly 1,400 people and left thousands missing. Scientists say decades of warming helped set the disaster in motion.

weekly.title: UK: Village votes to 'secede' in asylum center plan protest
weekly.summary: Residents of Piddington, a tiny, remote village in Oxfordshire in England, have staged a "referendum" on leaving the UK. They are objecting to plans to open an asylum reception center at a disused military base nearby.

weekly.title: Can Canada and the EU deepen ties to counter Trump?
weekly.summary: Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney is known for standing up to US President Donald Trump. Now he wants to forge a "unique alliance" with Europe. But what could such a partnership look like?

weekly.title: Chancellor Merz seeks CDU support amid far-right AfD surge
weekly.summary: Following the CDU's crushing defeat in the Saxony-Anhalt state election, many are expressing doubts about the party's leader, Chancellor Friedrich Merz. But the CDU doesn't appear to have a viable alternative.

weekly.title: Shock in Kosovo as Hague convicts former President Thaci
weekly.summary: The conviction in The Hague of former President Hashim Thaci and three former Kosovo Liberation Army leaders has caused consternation in Kosovo — both among political leaders and on the streets. DW reports from Pristina.

weekly.title: British-American writer Bonnie Greer dies aged 77
weekly.summary: Chicago-born playwright Bonnie Greer, who became a familiar face in British political discourse later in life, has died. Her husband David Hutchins announced news of Greer's death.

weekly.title: After Neuer: Who will be Germany's new No. 1 goalkeeper?
weekly.summary: Following Manuel Neuer's retirement, there are many candidates to succeed him, but which goalkeeper will Jürgen Klopp choose? What factors will play a role? And will Neuer's future have an indirect influence?

weekly.title: Poland reaffirms support for Ukraine after drone strikes
weekly.summary: After Russia's recent drone attacks on targets close to the Ukraine-Poland border, Warsaw has doubled down on its support for Kyiv and pledged a "nonprovocative but serious response" to Moscow.

weekly.title: Global Gender Gap Report: Women's hard-won gains 'fragile'
weekly.summary: Two decades of progress toward gender parity is at risk as women's political representation declines, according to a new World Economic Forum report. At the current pace, the remaining gap could take 120 years to close.

weekly.title: Kosovo ex-president Thaci sentenced to 25 years for war crimes
weekly.summary: A Hague tribunal ruled that Hashim Thaci, a former leader of the Kosovo Liberation Army (KLA), is responsible for war crimes carried out during the war of independence with Serbia.

weekly.title: German drama 'Blindspot Berlin' revisits 2016 Christmas market attack
weekly.summary: A decade after the terrorist attack on a Berlin Christmas market, a new German miniseries looks into the institutional failures that allowed the deadly truck rampage to happen.

weekly.title: How extreme heat is hitting wallets
weekly.summary: Heat waves, wildfires and floods have cascading economic impacts, causing incomes to decline and the price of basic goods to rise. The trend will escalate as temperatures continue to increase.

developing.title: India news: PM Modi says developing nations unfairly blamed for emissions
developing.summary: PM Narendra Modi has told a climate conference that developed countries emit six times more CO2 than India. Meanwhile, an IIT Bombay professor has been accused of caste abuse. DW has more.
